provenance.paper_title: Learning to Forget -- Hierarchical Episodic Memory for Lifelong Robot Deployment

representation_paths.memory_component: hierarchical scene instants, events and summaries

evidence.section: Full paper: Task and Architecture Overview
evidence.paraphrase: Online construction builds a history tree from scene instants to long-range summaries.

evidence.section: Full paper: Task and Architecture Overview
evidence.paraphrase: Lower-level events are summarized upward. For H2-EMV, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of hierarchical scene instants, events and summaries.

evidence.section: Full paper: Task and Architecture Overview
evidence.paraphrase: Tiered expiry and relevance remove detail while keeping placeholders. For H2-EMV, this specifically supports progressive decay of stored importance or retention of hierarchical scene instants, events and summaries.

evidence.section: Full paper: Task and Architecture Overview
evidence.paraphrase: User feedback updates natural-language retention rules used on later experience. The persistent later-use effect is deployment-feedback evolution of the reusable maintenance policy.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF pp. 13, 18, 21): User feedback during ongoing deployment revises reusable relevance rules that govern later summarization and forgetting, satisfying strict T3 maintenance-policy evolution. The qualifying feedback occurs during deployment/inference and affects later use.
